scoringCalibration: The score is rebased against fixed front, three-quarter, left, right, back and extreme-top renders. The new layered fibers improve the ordinary front and profile silhouette, but the exposed forehead band, repetitive curtain rhythm, rear split and extreme-top ribbon fan are production-blocking defects. Hair and face receive no near-finished credit while those defects remain visible.
visualFindings: The front and three-quarter silhouette now reads as continuous straight hair instead of sparse comb teeth and detached crown strips.
Staggered scalp-leave points and tangent-preserving cubic paths remove the hard horizontal helmet rim found by the new profile cameras.
The scalp density layer retains its feathered alpha edge while using a darker root tone, so the hairline no longer appears as a bright gray cap.
The dedicated 588-strand LOD preserves the front silhouette in a fixed-camera render while reducing the complete asset by 23 percent.
rejectedExperiments: v53 was rejected because pruning 32 cross-flow guides and shifting old strand roots did not materially improve the front view or crown coverage.
v54 was rejected because a small number of wide overlapping cards produced a helmet-like crown and striped rear gaps.
An opaque seven-card rear underlay was rejected because it created visible black strips with hard tips instead of closing the rear flow naturally.
blockingFailures: The extreme top view exposes a radial fan of ribbon tips and fails the production silhouette gate.
The forehead density band is too broad and geometric, while the front hairline lacks believable irregular recession and transition fibers.
The side lengths still read as a repetitive vertical curtain and need larger clump hierarchy, flyaways and ear-aware grouping.
The rear center still has a visible vertical separation and needs a more irregular overlapping root field.
Hair shading still needs an engine-side dual-lobe anisotropic model and strand-scale roughness variation.
The face still needs expression-oriented perioral loops, asymmetric commissure sculpting and a phoneme pose suite.
Integrated upper and lower eyelid thickness and expression-compatible canthus topology remain below review quality.
Clothing edge flow, seams, folds, materials and outer layers remain below review quality.
Raised-arm shoulders still require corrective deformation and the standard pose suite remains incomplete.
Signed clothing-distance samples remain negative despite zero exact triangle overlaps in the audited frames.
LOD transition popping and frame-time impact remain untested in the website renderer.
